title: Janapada of Malla
capsule: The Malla janapada occupied the eastern Himalayan foothills of what is now Kushinagar district, Uttar Pradesh, divided into two aristocratic republics—gaṇasaṅghas—with capitals at Kusīnārā and Pāvā. Both branches were governed by hereditary kṣatriya assemblies whose members held the collective title rājā; inner councils of four (Kusīnārā) and five (Pāvā) members handled executive functions. Kusīnārā is of particular Buddhist significance as the site of the Buddha's parinirvāṇa (c. 483 BCE), and Pāvā was the site of Mahāvīra's death. After prolonged warfare, Ajātaśatru of Magadha defeated the Vajjika League by around 468 BCE, absorbing the Mallas, who ceased to function as an independent republic before or during Mauryan rule.
